claims.text: The target material is a Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy in a solid-solution state.
The target state is at temperatures near melting.
An MTP for MoNbTaW can be trained using DFT data from elemental, binary, ternary, and quaternary systems in the Nb-Ta-Mo-W chemical space.
The proposed MTP training set includes explicit liquid-phase and high-temperature disordered configurations.
Full thermodynamic integration can be replaced by free energy perturbation using an MTP.
The proposed calculations use 2000-3000 K, 1 atm, more than 1000 atoms, a 1 fs time step, a 4.7 Å MTP cutoff, and MTP level 14.
MTPs construct rotationally invariant descriptors of local atomic environments and use a polynomial or linear basis expansion to represent atomic energies.
The proposed MTP captures local chemical short-range order.
The proposed MTP captures the liquid structure of multicomponent refractory alloys.
FEP obtains the solid-liquid free-energy difference through exponential averaging of energy differences over MTP-sampled states.
FEP avoids the slow convergence associated with full thermodynamic-integration paths.
MTPs can provide accuracy near that of their underlying DFT calculations while balancing accuracy and computational cost.
The MTP-FEP scheme will resolve melting free-energy differences within 5 meV/atom.
The MTP-FEP scheme will reduce computational cost by a factor of 10-100 relative to thermodynamic integration.
The cost reduction will enable high-throughput screening of Ta-based HEA compositions.
Empirical potentials such as EAM fail to capture liquid structure in multicomponent systems.
The method is valid within the Ta-Nb-Mo-W-V training-set chemical space but fails for extreme compositions or elements absent from training.
Omitting liquid and high-temperature disordered configurations can cause MTP extrapolation artifacts in liquid states.
Sparse liquid-phase DFT training data may increase free-energy uncertainty by 20-50%.
Deviation exceeding 10 meV/atom from direct AIMD thermodynamic integration is the proposed falsification criterion for the MTP-FEP method.
